statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: A host MAY implement a "half-duplex" TCP close sequence, so that an application that has called CLOSE cannot continue to read data from the connection (MAY-1).

statements.subject: tcp
statements.description: If such a host issues a CLOSE call while received data is still pending in the TCP connection, or if new data is received after CLOSE is called, its TCP implementation SHOULD send a RST to show that data was lost (SHLD-3).
actions: send RST to indicate data was lost

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: When a connection is closed actively, it MUST linger in the TIME-WAIT state for a time 2xMSL (Maximum Segment Lifetime) (MUST-13).

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: However, it MAY accept a new SYN from the remote TCP endpoint to reopen the connection directly from TIME-WAIT state (MAY-2), if it: (1) assigns its initial sequence number for the new connection to be larger than the largest sequence number it used on the previous connection incarnation, and (2) returns to TIME-WAIT state if the SYN turns out to be an old duplicate.
actions: assign ISN greater than previous connection maximum sequence number
return to TIME-WAIT state if SYN is identified as old duplicate

statements.subject: tcp
statements.description: This algorithm for reducing TIME-WAIT is a Best Current Practice that SHOULD be implemented since Timestamp Options are commonly used, and using them to reduce TIME-WAIT provides benefits for busy Internet servers (SHLD-4).
actions: implement Timestamp Options-based TIME-WAIT reduction algorithm
